Programa de Nutrición para Mujeres, Bebés y Niños de Juniper Hollow / WIC Juniper Hollow provides nutrition appointments. Fernwater Smart Start Family Partnership / Smart Start Fernwater supplies lending-library toys and parenting groups.

Juniper Hollow Early Head Start Collaborative / Early Head Start Juniper Hollow accepted a referral; enrollment remains pending per Mom. Coordinator will verify availability. Parents authorized communication about routines and IFSP supports only. No agency attendance requirement was added. Family asked that appointments be grouped when possible because transportation depends on one shared vehicle. Coordinator documented this preference.

**Outcome 1 — Pedir ayuda y cosas necesarias**

By January 8, 2027, pt will request a desired item, action, or help during breakfast and play using a word, word approximation, gesture, or picture in 8/10 opportunities across consecutive routine samples. Baseline: 3/10 w/ mod cues.

Strategies: CG places desired items within view, offers a meaningful choice, waits, and responds promptly. Use Enhanced Milieu Teaching and focused stimulation during existing routines. Targets: "ayuda", "help", "abre", and "open". Adults accept either language and avoid requiring repetition before meeting the request.

SLP will coach parents to distinguish an independent request from an imitated response. Mom will note brief examples after breakfast when feasible. Success means fewer unresolved requests and easier participation, not a required spoken phrase length. Gestures remain valid communication.

**Outcome 2 — Compartir la comida y el juego**

By January 8, 2027, pt will participate in reciprocal exchanges during meals or pretend play for 3 of 5 opportunities w/ min cues. Baseline: 1 of 5 w/ max cues.

CG follows pt’s interest, comments briefly, and leaves space for a response. Use Hanen interaction strategies and naturalistic language intervention. Model targets "mi turno", "your turn", "rico", and "eat". A response may be looking, giving an object, gesturing, or vocalizing.

Dad will practice during bath and dinner. Sister may participate voluntarily; adults remain responsible for support. SLP will demonstrate, observe CG practice, and offer feedback. Family selected this outcome because shared routines currently stop when adults increase questions or expect a spoken answer immediately.

**Outcome 3 — Transiciones con menos frustración**

By January 8, 2027, pt will follow a familiar transition direction and communicate acceptance, refusal, or need for help in 4/5 opportunities w/ mod cues. Baseline: 2/5 w/ max cues.

CG uses a consistent picture, short spoken cue, and advance notice before cleanup, handwashing, or leaving home. Targets include "espera", "wait", "all done", and "terminé". Adults acknowledge refusal and offer supported choices when possible.

SLP will coordinate picture use across home and childcare. Staff will document which supports help pt enter the next activity. Communication practice does not replace direct adult supervision near exits. Family will judge progress by participation and recovery during transitions, alongside the opportunity counts. Coordinator will check whether materials are accessible to each CG.

**Outcome 4 — Caregiver confidence across languages**

By January 8, 2027, parents and backup CG will demonstrate the agreed strategies in 80% of observed opportunities during a selected routine w/ min cues. Baseline: 40% w/ mod cues.

SLP will use caregiver coaching: joint planning, observation, supported practice, reflection, and feedback. Adults may model in Spanish, English, or a natural mix. Example adult target: "abre, open the box". SLP will explain that family members do not need to translate every utterance.

CG will identify what worked and choose the next small adjustment. Written reminders will use pictures and brief bilingual phrases. Family requested feedback without correction in front of visitors; clinician agreed to discuss detailed coaching privately.

**Servicios y fechas**

Speech-language services through Sendero Claro Therapy: 1x/week, approx 45 minutes, home or childcare according to the agreed routine. Start October 15, 2026; planned end January 8, 2027. Rendering provider: Marisol Vega Serrano. Billing code 92507; modifier GN. Scheduling: 919-555-0182; clinician email m.vega@example.invalid.

Service coordination through Coordinación Fernwater remains monthly and as needed, from October 10, 2026 through January 8, 2027. CDSA Juniper Hollow retains IFSP oversight. No additional therapy was requested today. Visits will occur in natural environments identified by the family. Coordinator will document changes in location, provider availability, or family preference before revising the service grid.

**Revisión, consentimiento y próximos pasos**

Today’s coaching sample showed independent requests in 5/10 opportunities after CG slowed questions. This sample reflects one visit; the team will check carryover across routines. Mom stated, “Así sí puedo hacerlo; poquito durante el día.” Dad selected bath play for his practice routine.

Parents verbally agreed to the outcomes and service schedule; signatures remain pending on the fictional review form. Coordinator will obtain signatures and share the bilingual summary. Next review: January 8, 2027, 10:00 AM. Family requested a reminder before the visit.

North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program
IFSP Review / Revisión del plan familiar
Synthetic training record; all people, organizations, locations, and identifiers are fictional.

FAMILY AND RECORD INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN FAMILIAR

Field	Information
Child	Octavio Daniel Luján
Preferred name	Tavi
Date of birth	August 12, 2024
Age at review	26 months
Review date	October 12, 2026
Original IFSP date	April 20, 2026
Child record	MF-CDSA-260418
Medicaid member	638105742L
Mother	Mariela Luján
Father	Esteban Cruz
Home address	184 Lantern Finch Lane, Alderhaven, North Carolina 27864
County	Mossfern County
Home languages	Spanish and English
Preferred communication	Spanish for explanations; bilingual written summaries
Mother’s telephone	919-555-0142
Father’s telephone	252-555-0176
Family email	mariela.lujan@example.com

Participants confirmed that the review reflects family priorities. Both parents attended at home. The maternal aunt joined briefly with permission. The family requested that providers explain unfamiliar terms in Spanish before discussing choices. Written consent remains necessary before sharing this document with another agency. The parents selected home visits because communication concerns occur most often during meals, dressing, and evening transitions. They want strategies that fit their routines and do not require buying materials.

CONTACT TEAM / EQUIPO DE APOYO

Role	Name	Organization	Contact
Service coordinator	Ms. Celia Montoro	Lantern Valley CDSA Office	919-555-0121
Bilingual speech-language pathologist	Ms. Inés Valverde	Mariposa Bridge Pediatric Therapy, PLLC	ines.valverde@example.com
Primary pediatrician	Dr. Nora Beltrán	Rivermoss Children’s Hospital	252-555-0108
Audiologist	Dr. Elias Quintero	Rivermoss Hearing Center	252-555-0114
Childcare lead teacher	Ms. Paloma Ríos	Little Lantern Nest Childcare	919-555-0183
Care coordination email	Ms. Celia Montoro	Lantern Valley CDSA Office	celia.montoro@example.com

FAMILY CONTEXT / NUESTRA FAMILIA

Octavio lives with his parents and sister, Lina Cruz, who is 6 years old. His maternal grandmother, Beatriz Luján, visits most afternoons. His aunt, Camila Luján, provides care when work schedules overlap. The family’s dog, Chispa, often stays beside the highchair. Adults supervise all interactions with the dog.

Mom works nights at Alderhaven Linen Cooperative as a laundry machine operator. Her shift begins at 10:00 p.m. and ends at 6:00 a.m.. Dad works at Juniper Wheel Repair as a bicycle mechanic, usually starting at 8:30 a.m.. The family prefers appointments after Mom has slept. Changes to her shift sometimes affect visit attendance.

The parents describe strong support from relatives but limited transportation during weekday mornings. Their neighbor, Mr. Tomás Olvera, sometimes provides rides by prior arrangement. He does not receive clinical information. The family rents its home and reports a quiet kitchen corner suitable for play. They prefer practice during ordinary activities, con cosas que ya tenemos, rather than a separate homework period.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA MÉDICA

Mother reports delivery at Rivermoss Children’s Hospital on August 12, 2024, following spontaneous labor at 35 weeks, 4 days gestation. Birth weight was 2,410 g. Apgar scores were 7 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Dr. Leona Arce attended the delivery. Octavio received care in the Rivermoss Children’s Hospital NICU for feeding support and observation of breathing.

Dr. Mateo Serrano, the neonatologist, documented discharge on August 21, 2024. These details appear in the fictional discharge summary reviewed with parental consent. Mother recalls that bottle feeding required extra time. She reports no current choking, persistent coughing with meals, or prescribed feeding restrictions.

Dr. Nora Beltrán follows growth and general development. The last well visit occurred on September 18, 2026. An audiology report dated September 29, 2026 documented responses adequate for the listening tasks completed, with repeat assessment recommended if concerns change. No medication allergies were reported. The family will contact the pediatrician about new medical concerns. Speech services address functional communication; medical follow-up remains with the child’s physicians.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES / LO QUE NOS IMPORTA

Mother stated, “Quiero entender lo que necesita antes de que llore. Cuando llego del trabajo, estoy cansada, pero sí quiero ayudar. No quiero que todo sea repetir palabras.”

Father stated, “He knows where everything is. He takes my hand and shows me, pero cuando no entiendo, se enoja. I want him to ask for help and tell me when he is finished.”

Grandmother Beatriz Luján added, “Conmigo escucha español. Con su papá escucha los dos idiomas. Queremos seguir hablando como habla nuestra familia.”

The family’s first priority is smoother communication during meals. Their second priority is requesting help with toys and dressing. Their third priority is joining play with other children without adults guessing every need. They want adults to recognize gestures as communication while modeling useful words.

The parents do not want to remove Spanish from home routines. The clinician affirmed this preference and planned bilingual examples matched to each caregiver. A successful week, según la familia, would include fewer difficult transitions and more shared enjoyment. The family will judge progress by useful communication, not by how many words an adult can make the child repeat.

DAILY ROUTINES / UN DÍA EN CASA

Routine	Current participation	Family’s preferred change
Morning meal, around 7:15 a.m.	Points toward food; protests when choices are unclear	Offer choices and accept a gesture, sound, or word
Dressing, around 8:00 a.m.	Brings shoes; needs help with sleeves	Request assistance before frustration increases
Childcare arrival, around 9:00 a.m.	Holds a familiar toy; watches other children	Join one predictable greeting activity
Afternoon play, around 3:30 p.m.	Enjoys cars, containers, and animal figures	Take turns and communicate about an action
Evening meal, around 6:15 p.m.	Leaves the table when finished	Use an agreed signal for finishing
Bedtime, around 8:15 p.m.	Enjoys songs; resists ending active play	Understand a short, consistent transition sequence

At breakfast, Tavi approaches the refrigerator and leads an adult by the hand. Mother usually offers the expected food quickly. She would like to pause long enough for a clearer message, sin hacerlo esperar demasiado. During dressing, he participates when adults show the next item. He becomes upset when several spoken directions occur together.

At childcare, Ms. Paloma Ríos reports that he watches classmates Ari Salcedo and Nila Mercer before approaching their play. Classroom assistant Ms. Vera Solís reports that a duplicate toy supports initial participation. During home play, sister Lina enjoys rolling cars back and forth. Adults will support her role as a play partner without making her responsible for treatment.

OTHER AGENCIES / OTROS APOYOS

Agency or setting	County	Current involvement	Planned coordination
Willow Basket WIC Office	Mossfern County	Nutrition appointments and food benefits	Family will share questions directly
Cedar Path DSS Office	Mossfern County	Childcare subsidy case	Coordinator will help clarify renewal paperwork
Bright Acorn Smart Start Partnership	Mossfern County	Family activity resources	Offer bilingual play-group information
Sunbird Early Head Start Office	Mossfern County	Application pending	Confirm status after written permission
Alderhaven Grove Elementary School	Mossfern County	Sibling attends	No child-specific information requested

The family identified application paperwork as a source of stress. Ms. Celia Montoro will help organize questions and contact details during a coordinator call. The coordinator will not assume that enrollment or benefits are approved. Mother will decide which agencies may receive information.

The clinician employed by Mariposa Bridge can provide a brief routine summary after consent. Childcare staff requested examples they can use during snacks and outdoor play. The family prefers one shared strategy sheet, en inglés y español, rather than separate instructions from each provider.

COMMUNICATION REVIEW / OBSERVACIONES Y RESULTADOS

Assessment occurred on October 5, 2026, with review discussion on October 12, 2026. The clinician used the PLS-5 Spanish alongside caregiver interview, play observation, and a bilingual communication sample. The scores describe this fictional assessment and are considered with functional observations.

Measure	Result	Interpretation within this record
PLS-5 Spanish: Auditory Comprehension	Standard score 82; percentile 12	Understanding improves with familiar routines
PLS-5 Spanish: Expressive Communication	Standard score 76; percentile 5	Spoken messages remain limited
PLS-5 Spanish: Total Language	Standard score 78; percentile 7	Communication support remains indicated
Total Language confidence interval	73–85	Reflects measurement uncertainty
Functional requesting sample	4/10 independent opportunities	Most requests used pointing or leading
Familiar routine directions	7/10 with min cues	Visual context supported participation
Shared play turns	3 of 5 with mod cues	Adult pacing supported engagement

Observed productions included “ma” while reaching toward food, “agua” near a cup, and “go” during car play. A sample entry coded [EW] reflected an incomplete word attempt. These productions were accepted as meaningful when context was clear. Consonant observations included /m/, /b/, and [w]. The clinician did not establish a separate speech sound treatment target from this brief sample.

PLAN PRINCIPLES / CÓMO VAMOS A PRACTICAR

The clinician will use Enhanced Milieu Teaching within family-selected routines. Strategies include following the child’s interest, modeling short messages, pausing, and responding to communication attempts. Caregivers will practice with coaching and immediate feedback. Models may be Spanish, English, or a natural combination that fits the caregiver.

Adults will offer assistance promptly when frustration rises. They will not withhold food or comfort to require speech. A gesture, picture, sound, or word can meet the communication purpose. The team will track useful messages across caregivers and settings. Family observations will guide adjustments.

OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES / RESULTADOS FAMILIARES

Outcome 1: Communicate a choice during meals.

By January 12, 2027, Octavio will communicate a food or drink choice in 8/10 naturally occurring opportunities across two caregivers, using a gesture, picture, sound, or word with min cues. Mother selected breakfast and the evening meal as practice routines.

Adults will show two available choices, name each briefly, and pause. Suggested models include “agua,” “milk,” and “quiero más.” The adult will honor the message and add a short model. If the child reaches without looking, the adult can still respond and model language. Caregivers will record examples on a simple tally sheet. Review will consider whether choices feel easier for the family.

Outcome 2: Request help during play and dressing.

By January 12, 2027, Tavi will request assistance in 4 of 5 opportunities across play and dressing, with min cues. Acceptable messages include giving an object, pointing, a help gesture, or a spoken attempt.

Father will model “help” when a toy container is difficult to open. Aunt Camila Luján will model “ayuda” during shoes and sleeves. Adults will notice early signs of difficulty, offer one model, and wait briefly. They will provide help if waiting increases distress. The clinician will coach adults to reduce prompts as messages become clearer. Progress includes easier recovery when a message is misunderstood.

Outcome 3: Participate in shared play.

By January 12, 2027, Octavio will complete 4 of 5 shared play turns with an adult or peer using min cues. A turn can include rolling a car, passing an animal figure, or adding a block.

The clinician will begin with familiar play and predictable actions. Models include “my turn,” “tu turno,” and “go.” At childcare, Ms. Paloma Ríos will offer short paired play with Ari Salcedo when both children are interested. Staff will avoid requiring eye contact before a turn. The family will report whether shared play becomes enjoyable and easier to sustain.

Outcome 4: Communicate completion and manage transitions.

By January 12, 2027, Tavi will use an agreed completion signal during meals or play in 80% of observed opportunities with min cues. The family chose a hand gesture paired with “all done” or “terminé.”

Adults will acknowledge the signal and explain the next activity using a short phrase and an object cue. At bedtime, they will use the same sequence of cleanup, book, and song. The clinician will help the family adjust wording if the sequence feels cumbersome. Progress will include clearer messages and fewer adult guesses. The team will record context when a transition remains difficult.

SERVICE SCHEDULE / SERVICIOS ACORDADOS

Service	Provider	Location	Frequency	Start date	End date	Session time
Speech-language intervention	Ms. Inés Valverde, MBPT	Family home	Weekly, 45 minutes	October 19, 2026	January 11, 2027	1:00 p.m.–1:45 p.m.
Service coordination	Ms. Celia Montoro	Home or telephone	Monthly and as needed	October 12, 2026	January 12, 2027	Planned call at 2:00 p.m.
Childcare consultation	Ms. Inés Valverde	Little Lantern Nest Childcare	Monthly, 30 minutes	October 26, 2026	January 11, 2027	9:30 a.m.–10:00 a.m.

Administrative coding: CPT 92507, modifier GN, and ICD-10 F80.2. Authorization reference: MBPT-SLP-261019-A. Coding does not replace the family outcomes or determine whether an individual visit occurred.

VISIT REVIEW / REVISIÓN DE LA VISITA

The review session began at 1:00 p.m. and ended at 2:05 p.m.. During coached snack practice, Octavio communicated choices in 5/8 opportunities with mod cues. Mother identified his pointing before the clinician prompted her. Father practiced a shorter model and reported that the pause felt manageable.

Compared with the previous family report, caregivers described more purposeful pointing and better participation with familiar songs. They still need support recognizing early requests for help. The team retained the family’s meal priority and added explicit completion signals. No provider reported that every outcome had been met.

The next review is scheduled for January 12, 2027. Ms. Celia Montoro will confirm the location and invite approved participants. The clinician will bring examples from completed visits, including the support needed. The parents will share which strategies fit their week and which need adjustment.

FAMILY AGREEMENT / ACUERDO

Mother Mariela Luján stated, “Este plan sí cabe en nuestro día. Podemos practicar mientras comemos y jugamos.” Father Esteban Cruz agreed to try the help model during evening play. The family received a bilingual copy and contact information for scheduling changes.

Prepared by Ms. Inés Valverde, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist, Mariposa Bridge Pediatric Therapy, PLLC.
